rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed concerning leading Quraysh opponents who had failed to match the Quran and assembled to challenge Muhammad; al-Qurtubi gives their names.
rows.anchor: الآية نزلت في رؤساء قريش مثل عتبة وشيبة ابني ربيعة، وأبي سفيان والنضر بن الحارث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs reproached Muhammad for disrupting their community and offered wealth, leadership, kingship, or treatment if his message came from a jinn companion.
rows.anchor: لقد شتمت الآباء وعبت الدين وشتمت الآلهة وسفهت الأحلام وفرقت الجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad answered that God had sent him as messenger with a book, glad tidings, and warning; he would patiently await God's judgment if they rejected him.
rows.anchor: ولكن الله بعثني إليكم رسولا وأنزل علي كتابا وأمرني أن أكون لكم بشيرا ونذيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They demanded that mountains be moved, their land widened with rivers, and deceased ancestors including Qusay be raised so they could verify Muhammad's claim.
rows.anchor: فليسير عنا هذه الجبال التي قد ضيقت علينا، وليبسط لنا بلادنا وليخرق لنا فيها أنهارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They then asked for an angel companion and gardens, palaces, and treasure that would spare Muhammad from earning his living; he again refused to request these things.
rows.anchor: سل ربك أن يبعث معك ملكا يصدقك بما تقول ويراجعنا عنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When they demanded the sky fall in pieces, Muhammad said that was God's decision; they alleged a man in Yamama called al-Rahman taught him and threatened him.
rows.anchor: ذلك إلى الله عز وجل إن شاء أن يفعله بكم فعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One opponent said they worship angels, while another demanded that Muhammad bring God and the angels visibly before them.
rows.anchor: وقال قائلهم: نحن نعبد الملائكة وهي بنات الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abd Allah ibn Abi Umayya challenged Muhammad to climb a ladder to heaven and return with a written attestation witnessed by four angels, while claiming he still would not believe.
rows.anchor: فوالله لا أؤمن بك أبدا حتى تتخذ إلى السماء سلما، ثم ترقى فيه وأنا أنظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad returned to his family saddened by the chiefs' rejection after he had hoped their invitation signaled openness.
rows.anchor: وانصرف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى أهله حزينا آسفا لما فاته مما كان يطمع به

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi identifies the preceding account of Quraysh's demands as Ibn Ishaq's wording and reports al-Wahidi's revelation account from Ikrima and Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: كله لفظ ابن إسحاق. وذكر الواحدي عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس:

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Yanbu means springs or water sources; the word follows the yafuul pattern from the verb meaning to spring forth.
rows.anchor: ينبوعا } يعني العيون عن مجاهد. وهي يفعول، من نبع ينبع.

rows.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers lighten tafjura; Abu Hatim prefers that reading because yanbu is singular, while Abu Ubayd favors matching the following intensified verb.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي «تفجر لنا» مخففة واختاره أبو حاتم

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abu Hatim distinguishes the verbs: the first precedes a singular spring, whereas the second precedes plural rivers, where intensification conveys abundance.
rows.anchor: لأن الأولى بعدها ينبوع وهو واحد، والثانية بعدها الأنهار وهي جمع، والتشديد يدل على التكثير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection to lightening the first verb is answered because yanbu, though singular, can intend a collective, as Mujahid's gloss indicates.
rows.anchor: أجيب بأن «ينبوعا» وإن كان واحدا فالمراد به الجمع، كما قال مجاهد.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reads the phrase as 'or you have a garden.'
rows.anchor: وقرأ قتادة «أو يكون لك جنة».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khilalaha means through the middle of the garden.
rows.anchor: خلالها } أي وسطها. { أو تسقط

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The common reading makes the addressee cause the sky to fall; Mujahid's reading attaches the verb directly to the sky.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد «أو يسقط السماء» على إسناد الفعل إلى السماء.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
rows.claim: Kasafan means pieces; with fatḥa on the sīn it is the plural of kisfa, the reading of Nafi, Ibn Amir, and Asim.
rows.anchor: كسفا } قطعا عن ابن عباس وغيره. والكسف بفتح السين جمع كسفة، وهي قراءة نافع وابن عامر وعاصم.

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says the first vocalization makes kasaf a singular and the other makes it plural.
rows.anchor: قال الأخفش: من قرأ كسفا من السماء جعله واحدا، ومن قرأ كسفا جعله جمعا.

rows.speaker: المهدوي
rows.claim: With a still sīn, kasaf may be a plural of kisfa or a verbal noun implying that a covering slab fall on them.
rows.anchor: قال المهدوي: ومن أسكن السين جاز أن يكون جمع كسفة وجاز أن يكون مصدرا

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari defines kisfa as a piece of something, such as cloth, and records its plural forms and variant use with kasf.
rows.anchor: وقال الجوهري: الكسفة القطعة من الشيء يقال: أعطني كسفة من ثوبك،

rows.speaker: قتادة وابن جريج
rows.claim: Qatada and Ibn Jurayj explain qabilan as seeing God and the angels face to face.
rows.anchor: أي معاينة عن قتادة وابن جريج

rows.speaker: الضحاك وابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and Ibn Abbas explain qabilan as guarantors or sureties.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك وابن عباس: كفيلا.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil takes qabilan to mean witnesses.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: شهيدا. مجاهد: هو

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid understands qabilan as groups of angels arriving tribe by tribe.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: هو جمع القبيلة أي بأصناف الملائكة قبيلة قبيلة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zukhruf means gold here, while its root sense is adornment; the related word can describe decorated water patterns.
rows.anchor: أو يكون لك بيت من زخرف } أي من ذهب عن ابن عباس وغيره. وأصله الزينة.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says he learned what zukhruf meant from Ibn Masud's reading, 'a house of gold'; Quraysh objected to Muhammad's poverty.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: كنت لا أدري ما الزخرف حتى رأيته في قراءة ابن مسعود «بيت من ذهب»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tarqu means to ascend; raqiy and irtiqa are verbs for climbing, and ruqiyaka is the verbal noun meaning your ascent.
rows.anchor: أو ترقى في السمآء } أي تصعد يقال: رقيت في السلم أرقى رقيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their demand for a book was that God send a separate document to every man, as the Quran describes elsewhere.
rows.anchor: أي كتابا من الله تعالى إلى كل رجل منا كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: أهل مكة والشام
rows.claim: Meccan and Syrian readers make 'Say: Glory be to my Lord' a declaration by the Prophet, exalting God above incapacity or human objection.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل مكة والشام { قل سبحان ربي } يعني النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أي قال ذلك تنزيها لله

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers treat 'Say' as a command to Muhammad to tell them he is only a human messenger who follows revelation.
rows.anchor: الباقون «قل» على أمر أي قل لهم يا محمد { هل كنت } أي ما أنا «إلا بشرا رسولا»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative explanation takes the whole response as an expression of astonishment at the opponents' extreme disbelief and demands.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هذا كله تعجب عن فرط كفرهم واقتراحاتهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi rejects the objection that the answer is unconvincing: a human messenger cannot choose miracles, and earlier messengers did not fulfill every demand.
rows.anchor: وغلطوا لأنه أجابهم فقال: إنما أنا بشر لا أقدر على شيء مما سألتموني،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once messengers establish proof with the signs God gives, people cannot insist on further signs; otherwise humans would control divine decisions and select their own messengers.
rows.anchor: فإذا أقاموا عليهم الحجة لم يجب لقومهم أن يقترحوا غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guidance that came to people means messengers and scriptures from God calling them to Him.
rows.anchor: يعني الرسل والكتب من عند الله بالدعاء إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their only stated obstacle was the ignorant belief that God was too exalted to send a human messenger, so they ignored the miracle and refused to submit to someone like themselves.
rows.anchor: جهلا منهم. { أبعث الله بشرا رسولا } أي الله أجل من أن يكون رسوله من البشر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, the first an is accusative after omission of a preposition, and the second is nominative as the subject of mana.
rows.anchor: ف«أن» الأولى في محل نصب بإسقاط حرف الخفض. و«أن» الثانية في محل رفع ب«منع»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels are sent as messengers to angels; humans could not see an angel in its created form, so God specially enabled prophets to see them as a sign and miracle.
rows.anchor: أعلم الله تعالى أن الملك إنما يرسل إلى الملائكة لأنه لو أرسل ملكا إلى الآدميين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi links this argument to the parallel discussion in al-Anam about a requested angel and the consequence of sending one.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم في «الأنعام» نظير هذه الآية وهو قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is related that after hearing the Prophet say he was only a human messenger, Quraysh asked who could testify to his prophethood, and this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor:
يروى أن كفار قريش قالوا حين سمعوا قوله:
هل كنت إلا بشرا رسولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whom God guides are guided; if He leaves people astray, no other protector can guide them.
rows.anchor: أي لو هداهم الله لاهتدوا. { ومن يضلل فلن تجد لهم أوليآء من دونه } أي لا يهديهم أحد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation treats being gathered on faces as an Arabic idiom for being hurried toward Hell.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أن ذلك عبارة عن الإسراع بهم إلى جهنم من قول العرب:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi prefers the literal view that they are dragged face-first to Hell, as people are dragged in this life in extreme humiliation and punishment.
rows.anchor: الثاني: أنهم يسحبون يوم القيامة على وجوههم إلى جهنم كما يفعل في الدنيا

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: A man asked the Prophet whether a disbeliever is gathered on his face; the Prophet answered that the One who made him walk on two feet can make him walk on his face at resurrection; Bukhari and Muslim transmit it.
rows.anchor: أن رجلا قال: يا رسول الله، الذين يحشرون على وجوههم، أيحشر الكافر على وجهه؟

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: When told the prophetic answer, Qatada affirmed it by swearing by the Lord's might.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة حين بلغه: بلى وعزة ربنا. أخرجه البخاري ومسلم.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: They interpret blind, mute, and deaf as blindness to what benefits them, inability to argue, and deafness to benefit; on this view their senses remain intact.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس والحسن: أي عمي عما يسرهم، بكم عن التكلم بحجة، صم عما ينفعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says they are first gathered with these impairments, then regain sight, speech, and hearing in Hell, as other verses indicate.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنهم يحشرون على الصفة التي وصفهم الله بها ليكون ذلك زيادة في عذابهم،

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
rows.claim: Muqatil says they become blind, deaf, mute, and unable to understand when ordered to remain despised in Hell and not speak.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن سليمان: إذا قيل لهم:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says darkness blinds them on entering Hell, they fall silent when forbidden to speak, and the fire's roar deafens them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: عموا حين دخلوا النار لشدة سوادها، وانقطع كلامهم حين قيل لهم:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maw'ahum means their settled abode and dwelling place.
rows.anchor: مأواهم جهنم } أي مستقرهم ومقامهم.

rows.speaker: الضحاك وغيره
rows.claim: They gloss khabat as quieted or subsided.
rows.anchor: كلما خبت } أي سكنت عن الضحاك وغيره.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses khabat as extinguished, and al-Qurtubi gives the corresponding verb's usage for a fire going out.
rows.anchor: مجاهد طفئت. يقال: خبت النار تخبو خبوا أي طفئت،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Increasing the blaze means rekindling its flames; even when its activity subsides, the sufferers' pain and punishment are not reduced.
rows.anchor: زدناهم سعيرا } أي نارا تتلهب. وسكون التهابها من غير نقصان في آلامهم

none: The segment is a broken quotation fragment with no explanatory point.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment is for rejecting God's signs and denying that they would be resurrected after becoming bones and dust.
rows.anchor: ذلك جزآؤهم بأنهم كفروا بآياتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rufatan means dust or crumbled remains.
rows.anchor: وقالوا أإذا كنا عظاما ورفاتا } أي ترابا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation of the heavens and earth proves God's ability to recreate humans; their appointed term is certain.
rows.anchor: أولم يروا أن الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض قادر على أن يخلق مثلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One syntactic interpretation puts the creation of the heavens and earth and the setting of a certain term before the assertion of God's ability to recreate them.
rows.anchor: قيل: في الكلام تقديم وتأخير، أي أو لم يروا أن الله الذي خلق السموات والأرض،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation makes the appointed term the span of earthly life ending in death, whose certainty is observable.
rows.anchor: والأجل: مدة قيامهم في الدنيا ثم موتهم، وذلك ما لا شك فيه إذ هو مشاهد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation connects the promise of a term to Quraysh's challenge that the sky be dropped in pieces.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو جواب قولهم: { أو تسقط السمآء كما زعمت علينا كسفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations identify the appointed term with the Day of Resurrection, the time of resurrection, which should not be doubted.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ذلك الأجل هو وقت البعث، ولا ينبغي أن يشك فيه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers are the polytheists, who persist in denying that term and God's signs.
rows.anchor: فأبى الظالمون إلا كفورا } أي المشركون إلا جحودا بذلك الأجل وبآيات الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The treasures of God's mercy mean stores of provision; another, broader explanation takes them as all blessings.
rows.anchor: أي خزائن الأرزاق. وقيل: خزائن النعم، وهذا أعم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypothetical exposes human miserliness: even if people had abundance, they would withhold from fear of poverty, just as Quraysh sought springs to expand their livelihood.
rows.anchor: من البخل، وهو جواب قولهم: «لن نؤمن لك حتى تفجر لنا من الأرض ينبوعا»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation gives two reasons humans would not give as God gives: they must reserve what they need, and they fear becoming poor, whereas God is above both conditions.
rows.anchor: لأمرين: أحدهما: أنه لا بد أن يمسك منها لنفقته وما يعود بمنفعته.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada explain al-infaq here as poverty; language scholars also use several verbs for becoming short of money.
rows.anchor: والإنفاق في هذه الآية بمعنى الفقر قاله ابن عباس وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qatur means miserly and restrictive; qattara and related forms mean limiting a family's spending, with three verb forms recorded.
rows.anchor: وكان الإنسان قتورا } أي بخيلا مضيقا. يقال: قتر على عياله يقتر ويقتر قترا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan holds that the verse was revealed specifically about the polytheists.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أنها نزلت في المشركين خاصة قاله الحسن.

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority hold that its lesson is general, an interpretation also reported by al-Mawardi.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أنها عامة، وهو قول الجمهور وذكره الماوردي.

rows.speaker: صفوان بن عسال المرادي
rows.claim: A report in al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasai describes two Jews asking the Prophet about Moses' nine signs; he lists nine commands and adds a Sabbath injunction for Jews. Al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih.
rows.anchor:
عن صفوان بن عسال المرادي
" أن يهوديين قال أحدهما لصاحبه: اذهب بنا إلى هذا النبي نسأله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
rows.claim: They identify the nine signs as the staff, hand, tongue, sea, flood, locusts, lice, frogs, and blood, each a distinct sign.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس والضحاك: الآيات التسع: العصا واليد واللسان والبحر والطوفان والجراد والقمل

rows.speaker: الحسن والشعبي
rows.claim: Hasan and al-Shabi combine the five signs in al-Araf with Moses' hand and staff, years of drought, and reduced crops.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن والشعبي: الخمس المذكورة في «الأعراف» يعنيان الطوفان وما عطف عليه، واليد والعصا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: A version from Hasan counts drought and crop loss together, then makes the staff swallowing the magicians' illusion the ninth sign.
rows.anchor: إلا أنه يجعل السنين والنقص من الثمرات واحدة، وجعل التاسعة تلقف العصا ما يأفكون.

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik gives a similar count but substitutes the sea and the mountain for the years and crop losses.
rows.anchor: وعن مالك كذلك إلا أنه جعل مكان السنين والنقص من الثمرات: البحر والجبل.

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Kab counts the five signs in al-Araf, the sea, staff, stone, and the blighting of wealth.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب: هي الخمس التي في «الأعراف» والبحر والعصا والحجر والطمس على أموالهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to ask the Children of Israel is an inquiry for Jewish confirmation of what Moses brought, testing the truth of Muhammad's account.
rows.anchor: أي سلهم يا محمد إذ جاءهم موسى بهذه الآيات

rows.speaker: الفراء وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: They explain Pharaoh's calling Moses mashuran as calling him a sorcerer because of his extraordinary deeds; a passive form is used with an active meaning.
rows.anchor: أي ساحرا بغرائب أفعالك قاله الفراء وأبو عبيدة. فوضع المفعول موضع الفاعل

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil explains mashuran as deceived or overcome; other explanations were discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: وقيل مخدوعا. وقيل مغلوبا قاله مقاتل.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو نهيك
rows.claim: They read the verb as past tense: Moses asked Pharaoh to free the Children of Israel and let them leave with him.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس وأبي نهيك أنهما قرأا «فسأل بني إسرائيل» على الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nine signs were brought into existence by the Lord of the heavens and earth as proofs of His power and oneness.
rows.anchor: و«أنزل» بمعنى أوجد. { إلا رب السماوات والأرض بصآئر } أي دلالات يستدل بها على قدرته

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The common reading has Moses address Pharaoh with 'you knew'; al-Qurtubi says this best fits the sense and Ibn Abbas's proof from 27:14.
rows.anchor: وقراءة العامة «علمت» بفتح التاء، خطابا لفرعون.

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisai reads 'I knew,' with the pronoun referring to Moses; this reading is also attributed to Ali.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي بضم التاء، وهي قراءة علي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali is reported to argue that God's enemy Pharaoh did not know, but Moses did; Ibn Abbas counters with the verse saying they inwardly recognized the signs.
rows.anchor: وقال: والله ما علم عدو الله ولكن موسى هو الذي علم،

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd prefers the open-t reading for its contextual sense; he says the attribution to Ali is unestablished and derives only from unknown Kulthum al-Muradi.
rows.anchor: والمأخوذ به عندنا فتح التاء، وهو الأصح للمعنى الذي احتج به ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says Moses attributed knowledge to Pharaoh because Pharaoh knew magicians' limits and recognized Moses' signs as beyond sorcery.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنما أضاف موسى إلى فرعون العلم بهذه المعجزات لأن فرعون قد علم مقدار ما يتهيأ للسحرة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid recounts that Moses' staff became a serpent spanning the house, terrifying Pharaoh so badly that he soiled his cloak; faqm means jaw.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: دخل موسى على فرعون في يوم شات وعليه قطيفة له، فألقى موسى عصاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this threat, zann means certainty rather than conjecture; thubur can mean destruction or loss.
rows.anchor: الظن هنا بمعنى التحقيق. والثبور: الهلاك والخسران أيضا.

rows.speaker: المنهال عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس وأبان بن تغلب
rows.claim: They explain muthburan as accursed; Ibn al-Zibara's verse uses it in that sense.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ملعونا رواه المنهال عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس. وقاله أبان بن تغلب.

rows.speaker: ميمون بن مهران عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported through Maymun ibn Mihran to explain muthburan as deficient in intellect.
rows.anchor: وقال ميمون بن مهران عن ابن عباس: «مثبورا» ناقص العقل.

rows.speaker: قتادة والحسن ومجاهد
rows.claim: Qatada, Hasan, and Mujahid explain muthburan as doomed or destroyed; the root verb means to destroy an enemy.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة هالكا. وعنه أيضا والحسن ومجاهد: مهلكا. والثبور: الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lexical interpretation makes muthburan one prevented from good, based on the idiom 'what kept you from it'; the root has two conjugations.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ممنوعا من الخير. حكى أهل اللغة: ما ثبرك عن كذا أي ما منعك منه.

rows.speaker: ابن الزبعرى
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zibara's verse uses muthbur for someone following Satan's path, supporting the sense of loss or ruin.
rows.anchor: إذ أجاري الشيطان في سنن

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses muthburan as bewitched, returning Pharaoh's accusation with a different word.
rows.anchor: الضحاك: «مثبورا» مسحورا. رد عليه مثل ما قال له باختلاف اللفظ.

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says muthburan means mentally deranged or lacking reason.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: «مثبورا» مخبولا لا عقل له.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh intended to expel Moses and the Israelites from Egypt, by killing or banishing them, so God destroyed him by drowning.
rows.anchor: أي أراد فرعون أن يخرج موسى وبني إسرائيل من أرض مصر إما بالقتل أو بالإبعاد فأهلكه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Pharaoh drowned, God told the Israelites to settle in the land, meaning Syria and Egypt.
rows.anchor: أي من بعد إغراقه. { لبني إسرائيل اسكنوا الأرض } أي أرض الشأم ومصر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The latter promise means the Resurrection: people will be brought from their graves mixed together, strangers from different places who do not recognize or regroup with their tribes.
rows.anchor: أي القيامة { جئنا بكم لفيفا } أي من قبوركم مختلطين من كل موضع،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada gloss the gathering as everyone brought together from widely different directions; al-Qurtubi says the meaning is the same.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وقتادة: جئنا بكم جميعا من جهات شتى. والمعنى واحد.

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari defines lafif as people gathered from various tribes and notes it also describes food mixed from two or more kinds; al-Asmai says it is a collective with no singular.
rows.anchor: قال الجوهري: واللفيف ما اجتمع من الناس من قبائل شتى

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi takes the latter promise to refer to Jesus' descent from heaven.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: «فإذا جاء وعد الآخرة» يعني مجيء عيسى عليه السلام من السماء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the Quran, connected to the earlier mention of signs and revelation.
rows.anchor: هذا متصل بما سبق من ذكر المعجزات والقرآن. والكناية ترجع إلى القرآن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation distinguishes the repetition: God made its descent obligatory in truth, and it descended containing truth, like someone going out clothed.
rows.anchor: معنى الأول: أوجبنا إنزاله بالحق. ومعنى الثاني: ونزل وفيه الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes the first bi as 'with' truth, while the second says the Quran descended upon Muhammad, as in the idiom 'I came to Zayd.'
rows.anchor: وقيل الباء في «وبالحق» الأول بمعنى مع، أي مع الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation says God decreed that the Quran descend in truth, and that it descended accordingly.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يجوز أن يكون المعنى وبالحق قدرنا أن ينزل، وكذلك نزل.

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh analyzes Quranan as an accusative governed by an implied verb explained by the following verb.
rows.anchor: مذهب سيبويه أن «قرآنا» منصوب بفعل مضمر يفسره الظاهر.

rows.speaker: جمهور الناس
rows.claim: The common light reading of farraqnahu means the Quran was clarified and truth distinguished from falsehood; Hasan gives this explanation and Ibn Abbas says it was divided into parts.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «فرقناه» بتخفيف الراء، ومعناه بيناه وأوضحناه،

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan glosses the Quran's separation as distinguishing truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: وفرقنا فيه بين الحق والباطل قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the light reading as dividing or detailing the Quran.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: فصلناه. وقرأ

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعلي وابن مسعود وأبي بن كعب وقتادة وأبو رجاء والشعبي
rows.claim: These authorities read the verb with a doubled r, meaning revelation came piece by piece rather than all at once; Ibn Masud and Ubay add 'to you.'
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وعلي وابن مسعود وأبي بن كعب وقتادة وأبو رجاء والشعبي «فرقناه» بالتشديد،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The reported descent period varies: Ibn Abbas says twenty-three years, Anas twenty, and another view twenty-five, reflecting disagreement about the Prophet's age; all agree it first descended to the lowest heaven at once.
rows.anchor: فقيل: في خمس وعشرين سنة. ابن عباس: في ثلاث وعشرين. أنس: في عشرين.

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن عباس وابن جريج
rows.claim: They interpret 'at a measured pace' as reciting without haste, giving each passage its due through measured, beautiful recitation without melody that alters the text; such alteration is forbidden.
rows.anchor: على ترسل في التلاوة وترتيل قاله مجاهد وابن عباس وابن جريج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the gradual-revelation reading, 'at a measured pace' means it came verse by verse and sura by sura; if all obligations arrived together, people would recoil.
rows.anchor: أي أنزلناه نجما بعد نجم ولو أخذوا بجميع الفرائض في وقت واحد لنفروا

rows.speaker: ابن محيصن
rows.claim: All readers except Ibn Muhaysin use a damma on the mīm of makth; he reads it with fatḥa, and three language forms are noted.
rows.anchor: وأجمع القراء على ضم الميم من «مكث» إلا ابن محيصن فإنه قرأ «مكث» بفتح الميم.

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik glosses 'at a measured pace' as deliberate, unhurried recitation.
rows.anchor: قال مالك: «على مكث» على تثبت وترسل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The instruction to believe or not believe addresses the Quran as rebuke and threat, not as a genuine choice.
rows.anchor: يعني القرآن. وهذا من الله عز وجل على وجه التبكيت لهم والتهديد لا على وجه التخيير.

rows.speaker: ابن جريج وغيره
rows.claim: Those given knowledge before the Quran are identified by one view as believing People of the Book; Ibn Jurayj understands 'when it is recited to them' as their scripture.
rows.anchor: وهم مؤمنو أهل الكتاب في قول ابن جريج وغيره

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj takes the recitation in this clause as their own scripture.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج: معنى { إذا يتلى عليهم } كتابهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies the learned with descendants of Ishmael who kept their religion until Muhammad, including Zayd ibn Amr and Waraqa ibn Nawfal; here knowledge means religious learning, not possession of scripture.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هم قوم من ولد إسماعيل تمسكوا بدينهم إلى أن بعث الله تعالى النبي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan identifies those given knowledge as Muhammad's community.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: الذين أوتوا العلم أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies them as Jews and says the Quran is recited to them; al-Qurtubi calls this more apparent because the verse says 'before him.'
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: إنهم ناس من اليهود وهو أظهر لقوله «من قبله».

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Jews heard the Quran, prostrated, and glorified God, affirming that God's promise would certainly be fulfilled.
rows.anchor: كانوا إذا سمعوا ما أنزل الله تعالى من القرآن سجدوا وقالوا: «سبحان ربنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says they recognized the promised prophet from the Torah, humbled themselves, and inclined toward Islam; the verse was revealed concerning them.
rows.anchor: هذا هو المذكور في التوراة، وهذه صفته، ووعد الله به واقع لا محالة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One group identifies the knowledgeable ones as Muhammad himself, with 'before him' referring to the Quran; another takes both pronouns as referring to Muhammad and begins the Quran's mention at 'when it is recited.'
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: المراد بالذين أوتوا العلم من قبله محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This passage is evidence that glorifying God in prostration is permissible; Aisha reports that the Prophet often said this supplication while bowing and prostrating.
rows.anchor: دليل على جواز التسبيح في السجود. وفي صحيح مسلم وغيره عن عائشة رضي الله عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their weeping is an emphatic commendation; anyone who has learned should respond to Quran by humility and submission.
rows.anchor: هذه مبالغة في صفتهم ومدح لهم. وحق لكل من توسم بالعلم

rows.speaker: التيمي
rows.claim: Al-Taymi says knowledge that does not make its possessor weep may not truly be knowledge, since God describes the learned this way; al-Tabari also transmits it.
rows.anchor: عن التيمي قال: من أوتي من العلم ما لم يبكه لخليق ألا يكون أوتي علما

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan explains adhqan as jaws, indicating that they place their jaws on the ground in prostration, the ultimate humility.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: الأذقان عبارة عن اللحى أي يضعونها على الأرض في حال السجود،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām can mean 'upon,' as in the idiom 'he fell on his mouth.'
rows.anchor: واللام بمعنى على تقول سقط لفيه أي على فيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says adhqan means faces; the chin is singled out because it is the nearest part of the face to the ground.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: «ويخرون للأذقان سجدا» أي للوجوه، وإنما خص الأذقان بالذكر

rows.speaker: ابن خويز منداد
rows.claim: Ibn Khuwazim says prostrating on the chin itself is impermissible: chin can stand for the face by adjacency or part-for-whole usage, as in poetry about falling face-first.
rows.anchor: قال ابن خويز منداد: ولا يجوز السجود على الذقن لأن الذقن ها هنا عبارة عن الوجه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Weeping from fear of God or grief over sin does not invalidate or harm prayer.
rows.anchor: دليل على جواز البكاء في الصلاة من خوف الله تعالى، أو على معصيته

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن الشخير
rows.claim: Abd Allah ibn al-Shikhkhir says he saw the Prophet praying while his chest rumbled like a boiling pot or mill from weeping; the report is cited from Ibn al-Mubarak and Abu Dawud.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه قال: أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يصلي ولجوفه أزيز كأزير المرجل

rows.speaker: مالك والثوري
rows.claim: Malik says moaning does not invalidate a sick person's prayer but dislikes it from a healthy person; al-Thawri agrees.
rows.anchor: فقال مالك: الأنين لا يقطع الصلاة للمريض، وأكرهه للصحيح وبه قال الثوري.

rows.speaker: ابن الحكم عن مالك
rows.claim: One report from Malik says throat-clearing, moaning, and blowing do not break prayer.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن الحكم عن مالك: التنحنح والأنين والنفخ لا يقطع الصلاة،

rows.speaker: ابن القاسم
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qasim holds that such sounds break prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن القاسم: يقطع. وقال

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafii says prayer is invalidated if the moan contains audible, intelligible letters.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي: إن كان له حروف تسمع وتفهم يقطع الصلاة.

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa says a moan from fear of God does not break prayer, but one from pain does.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: إن كان من خوف الله لم يقطع، وإن كان من وجع قطع.

rows.speaker: أبو يوسف
rows.claim: Abu Yusuf holds the prayer complete in all such cases because sick or weak people cannot avoid moaning.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي يوسف أن صلاته في ذلك كله تامة لأنه لا يخلو مريض ولا ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation of khushu has already been given in al-Baqara and will be revisited later.
rows.anchor: تقدم القول في الخشوع في «البقرة» ويأتي.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One occasion report says polytheists heard Muhammad invoke Allah and al-Rahman and accused him of calling on two gods despite preaching one.
rows.anchor: أن المشركين سمعوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يدعو «يا ألله يا رحمن» فقالوا:

rows.speaker: مكحول
rows.claim: Makhul says the Prophet invoked al-Rahman and al-Rahim at night; a listener associated al-Rahman with a man in Yamama, prompting the verse to clarify that Allah and al-Rahman name one deity.
rows.anchor: تهجد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة فقال في دعائه: «يا رحمن يا رحيم»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another occasion links the verse to the basmala: Quraysh recognized al-Rahim but asked who al-Rahman was after Muhammad wrote the formula.
rows.anchor: فكتب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم» فقال المشركون: هذا الرحيم نعرفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Jews asked why the Quran lacked the name al-Rahman, familiar from the Torah.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن اليهود قالت: ما لنا لا نسمع في القرآن اسما هو في التوراة

rows.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
rows.claim: Talha ibn Musarrif reads 'whichever you call' with man after ayyan, emphasizing that the Most Beautiful Names entail the finest attributes and meanings.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف «أيا من تدعوا فله الأسماء الحسنى»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's names are established by revelation or consensus; reason alone cannot invent a name for God.
rows.anchor: وهي بتوقيف لا يصح وضع اسم الله بنظر إلا بتوقيف من القرآن أو الحديث أو الإجماع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The first setting says the Prophet prayed loudly with companions in Mecca, so polytheists heard and insulted the Quran, its sender, and its bearer; he was told to be audible to companions without exposing the recitation to opponents.
rows.anchor: نزلت ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم متوار بمكة، وكان إذا صلى بأصحابه رفع صوته بالقرآن،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi cites the report as transmitted by Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, and others, with Muslim's wording; khafata means lowering the voice or becoming still.
rows.anchor: أخرجه البخاري ومسلم والترمذي وغيرهم. واللفظ لمسلم. والمخافتة: خفض الصوت والسكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poem is cited to illustrate khafata as a quiet breath or fading voice, and a faint or altered gaze.
rows.anchor:
لم يبق إلا نفس خافت
ومقلة إنسانها باهت

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha says the instruction about not raising or lowering the prayer was revealed concerning supplication.
rows.anchor: ما رواه مسلم أيضا عن عائشة في قوله عز وجل: { ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin's report about raised tashahhud implies that the verse calls for concealing it; Ibn Masud calls concealment the Sunna according to Ibn al-Mundhir.
rows.anchor: قلت: وعلى هذا فتكون الآية متضمنة لإخفاء التشهد، وقد قال ابن مسعود: من السنة أن تخفي التشهد

rows.speaker: أبو بكر وعمر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr recited quietly to converse privately with God, while Umar recited aloud to drive Satan away and wake sleepers; the verse directed Abu Bakr to raise his voice a little and Umar to lower his.
rows.anchor: يسر قراءته، وكان عمر يجهر بها،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: On the day-versus-night interpretation, optional prayers may be recited aloud or quietly at any time, while obligatory prayers have established recitation rules.
rows.anchor: فأما النوافل فالمصلي مخير في الجهر والسر في الليل والنهار

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan interprets the command as prohibiting ostentation in public while also forbidding neglect in private.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: يقول الله لا ترائي بصلاتك تحسنها في العلانية ولا تسيئها في السر.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also says not to pray for show or abandon prayer from fear of people.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: لا تصل مرائيا للناس ولا تدعها مخافة الناس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is used for recitation and recitation for prayer by metonymy, since the prayer includes reciting, bowing, and prostrating; the sound hadith on dividing prayer refers to reciting al-Fatiha.
rows.anchor: لأن الصلاة تشتمل على قراءة وركوع وسجود فهي من جملة أجزائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refutes Jews, Christians, and Arabs who separately claimed that Uzayr, Jesus, or the angels were God's children.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية رادة على اليهود والنصارى والعرب في قولهم أفذاذا: عزير وعيسى والملائكة ذرية الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has no partner because He alone rules and is worshipped.
rows.anchor: لأنه واحد لا شريك له في ملكه ولا في عبادته

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains 'no ally from humiliation' as God neither forming an alliance nor seeking anyone's help; He has no protector against humiliation.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: المعنى لم يحالف أحدا ولا ابتغى نصر أحد

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says God has no ally among Jews or Christians, rejecting their claim to be God's children and beloved ones.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: لم يكن له ولي من اليهود والنصارى لأنهم أذل الناس،

rows.speaker: الحسن بن الفضل
rows.claim: Hasan ibn al-Fadl says God is never humiliated and needs no protector or helper because of His might and majesty.
rows.anchor: يعني لم يذل فيحتاج إلى ولي ولا ناصر لعزته وكبريائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kabbirhu means magnify God completely; Allahu akbar is the Arabs' strongest expression of exaltation, declaring Him greater than everything.
rows.anchor: أي عظمة تامة. ويقال: أبلغ لفظة للعرب في معنى التعظيم والإجلال: الله أكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi cites a poem illustrating that God is greater than everything and most numerous in forces.
rows.anchor:
رأيت الله أكبر كل شيء
محاولة وأكثرهم جنودا

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar says a servant's saying Allahu akbar is better than the world and everything in it.
rows.anchor: وقال عمر بن الخطاب: قول العبد الله أكبر خير من الدنيا وما فيها.

rows.speaker: مطرف عن عبد الله بن كعب
rows.claim: A report says this is the Torah's closing verse, while its opening was the beginning of al-Anam.
rows.anchor: روى مطرف عن عبد الله بن كعب قال: افتتحت التوراة بفاتحة سورة الأنعام وختمت بخاتمة هذه السورة.

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: A report from Muadh ibn Jabal attributes to the Prophet the description of this as the verse of might.
rows.anchor:
وفي الخبر:
" أنها آية العز "
رواه معاذ بن جبل عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم.

rows.speaker: عمرو بن شعيب عن أبيه عن جده
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet taught this verse to a boy of Banu Abd al-Muttalib once he could speak clearly.
rows.anchor: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أفصح الغلام من بني عبد المطلب علمه «وقل الحمد لله

rows.speaker: عبد الحميد بن واصل
rows.claim: Abd al-Hamid ibn Wasil reports a reward like the earth and mountains for reciting this verse, because another verse depicts the heavens, earth, and mountains recoiling from claims of divine offspring.
rows.anchor: من قرأ وقل الحمد لله الآية كتب الله له من الأجر مثل الأرض والجبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet instructed a man burdened by debt to recite the sura from 'Call upon Allah or call upon al-Rahman' to its end, then repeat a trust in the Ever-Living three times.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أمر رجلا شكا إليه بالدين بأن يقرأ «قل ادعوا الله أو ادعوا الرحمن»

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Quraysh sent al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and Uqba ibn Abi Muayt to Jewish scholars, who advised asking about the cave youths, the world-traveling ruler, and the Spirit as tests of Muhammad's prophethood.
rows.anchor:
ذكر ابن إسحاق:
" أن قريشا بعثوا النضر بن الحارث وعقبة بن أبي معيط إلى أحبار يهود

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: The two men returned to Mecca, asked the three questions, and Muhammad promised an answer the next day without saying 'if God wills'; revelation then stopped for fifteen nights, provoking mockery and distress.
rows.anchor: فقال لهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أخبركم بما سألتم عنه غدا» ولم يستثن.

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Gabriel eventually brought the Cave sura with the answers and a rebuke over Muhammad's grief; when Muhammad complained of the delay, Gabriel cited that descent occurs only by God's command.
rows.anchor: ثم جاءه جبريل عليه السلام من عند الله عز وجل بسورة أصحاب الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura opens with praise and confirms Muhammad's prophethood in response to those who denied it: God sent the Book upon His servant.
rows.anchor: فافتتح السورة تبارك وتعالى بحمده، وذكر نبوة رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما أنكروا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book has no crookedness and is upright, with no inconsistency.
rows.anchor: أي معتدلا لا اختلاف فيه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book warns of immediate punishment in this world and painful punishment in the next, from the Lord who sent Muhammad.
rows.anchor: لينذر بأسا شديدا من لدنه } أي عاجل عقوبته في الدنيا، وعذابا أليما في الآخرة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who affirm what Muhammad brought and do righteous deeds receive a good reward: the everlasting Garden, where they never die.
rows.anchor: أي دار الخلد لا يموتون فيها، الذين صدقوك بما جئت به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The specific warning targets Quraysh's claim that angels are God's daughters.
rows.anchor: يعني قريشا في قولهم: إنا نعبد الملائكة وهي بنات الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They and their forebears have no evidence for the claim; it is a grave utterance of falsehood from their mouths.
rows.anchor: ما لهم به من علم ولا لآبائهم } الذين أعظموا فراقهم وعيب دينهم.

rows.speaker: ابن هشام
rows.claim: Ibn Hisham, citing Abu Ubayda, glosses bakhia nafsak as destroying or killing oneself; the idiom also means exhausting oneself for someone.
rows.anchor: قال ابن هشام: «باخع نفسك» مهلك نفسك فيما حدثني أبو عبيدة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was grieving the people's rejection after they turned away; the verse tells him not to destroy himself with sorrow.
rows.anchor: لحزنه عليهم حين فاته ما كان يرجوه منهم، أي لا تفعل.

rows.speaker: ذو الرمة
rows.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's poem uses bakhia for someone consuming himself with grief, serving as linguistic evidence for the word.
rows.anchor:
ألا أيهذا الباخع الوجد نفسه
بشيء نحته عن يديه المقادر

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq explains the trial as testing who follows God's command and obeys Him best.
rows.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: أي أيهم أتبع لأمري وأعمل بطاعتي.

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: What is on earth will perish; all return to God for recompense, so the Prophet should not grieve over what he sees or hears.
rows.anchor: المرجع إلي فأجزي كلا بعمله

rows.speaker: ابن هشام
rows.claim: Ibn Hisham defines saeid as the earth's surface and cites Dhu al-Rumma's line as poetic usage; it also means a road, as in a hadith.
rows.anchor: قال ابن هشام: الصعيد وجه الأرض، وجمعه صعد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith warning against sitting on saeid refers to roads, and jarz is barren land that produces nothing, including a drought-stricken year.
rows.anchor:
إياكم والقعود على الصعدات "
يريد الطرق. والجرز: الأرض التي لا تنبت شيئا،

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the cave youths were not the most astonishing of God's signs; other proofs among His creatures are more wondrous.
rows.anchor: أم حسبت أن أصحاب الكهف والرقيم كانوا من آياتنا عجبا

rows.speaker: ابن هشام
rows.claim: Ibn Hisham defines al-Raqim as the inscribed record of their story and says its plural is raqam; al-Ajjaj's verse supplies the word marqam.
rows.anchor: قال ابن هشام: والرقيم الكتاب الذي رقم بخبرهم، وجمعه رقم.

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq presents their account as true: they believed in their Lord, were given guidance, and had their hearts strengthened when they declared God alone Lord of heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: نحن نقص عليك نبأهم بالحق } أي بصدق الخبر { إنهم فتية آمنوا بربهم

rows.speaker: ابن هشام
rows.claim: Ibn Hisham explains shatat as excess and departure from truth; a verse by al-Asha of Banu Qays ibn Thalaba supports the usage.
rows.anchor: قال ابن هشام: والشطط الغلو ومجاوزة الحق.

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says their people had no clear proof for worshipping other gods besides God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: أي بحجة بالغة.

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: When the youths withdrew to the cave, God would extend mercy and arrange their affairs; the sun's path avoided them while they lay in its spacious interior.
rows.anchor: فأووا إلى الكهف ينشر لكم ربكم من رحمته ويهيىء لكم من أمركم مرفقا

rows.speaker: ابن هشام
rows.claim: Ibn Hisham glosses tazawwar as turning aside, from zawr; Abu al-Zahf al-Kulaybi's verse attests the form azwar.
rows.anchor: قال ابن هشام: تزاور تميل وهو من الزور.

rows.speaker: ابن هشام
rows.claim: Ibn Hisham says taqriduhum means the sun passed them and left them on its left; Dhu al-Rumma's verse illustrates the verb.
rows.anchor: و«تقرضهم ذات الشمال» تجاوزهم وتتركهم عن شمالها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fajwa means open space or breadth; its plural is faja, with a poem illustrating the word.
rows.anchor: والفجوة: السعة، وجمعها الفجاء. قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account is a sign proving Muhammad's truth to the People of the Book who prompted Quraysh's questions, because it verifies their story.
rows.anchor: أي في الحجة على من عرف ذلك من أمورهم من أهل الكتاب ممن أمر هؤلاء بمسألتك

rows.speaker: ابن هشام
rows.claim: Ibn Hisham defines al-wasid as the door; it can also mean a courtyard and has the plural forms wasa id, wasd, and wasdan.
rows.anchor: قال ابن هشام: الوصيد الباب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The group with authority were those who prevailed in the affair, and the ones who will say 'build over them a place of worship' are the Jewish scholars who sent Quraysh to ask.
rows.anchor: الذين غلبوا على أمرهم } أهل السلطان والملك منهم. { لنتخذن عليهم مسجدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three- and five-youth counts are speculation, while the seven-count is followed by a command to say God knows best and not to dispute or consult the Jews.
rows.anchor: ويقولون سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم قل ربي أعلم بعدتهم ما يعلمهم إلا قليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command not to debate means avoid disputing them beyond an outward discussion, and do not consult people who lack knowledge of the youths.
rows.anchor: أي لا تكابرهم { إلا مرآء ظاهرا ولا تستفت فيهم منهم أحدا } فإنهم لا علم لهم بهم.

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: The Prophet should not promise tomorrow's answer without invoking God's will; after forgetting, remember God and ask Him to guide you to the more correct answer.
rows.anchor: واذكر ربك إذا نسيت وقل عسى أن يهدين ربي لأقرب من هذا رشدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that they remained 309 years is something people will say; God knows their duration and the unseen of heaven and earth, with no partner in His judgment.
rows.anchor: أي سيقولون ذلك. { قل الله أعلم بما لبثوا له غيب السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: الأخفش والكسائي والفراء وأبو عبيد وجمهور المتأولين
rows.claim: They analyze the opening as reordered: God sent the upright Book and did not make it crooked, with qayyiman in the accusative as a circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: وزعم الأخفش والكسائي والفراء وأبو عبيد وجمهور المتأولين أن في أول هذه السورة تقديمًا وتأخيرًا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reads the words in their stated order, supplying the sense 'He did not make it crooked, but made it upright.'
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: الكلام على سياقه من غير تقديم ولا تأخير،

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi commends al-Dahhak's explanation: the Book is upright in wisdom, with no error, corruption, or contradiction.
rows.anchor: وقول الضحاك فيه حسن، وأن المعنى: مستقيم، أي مستقيم الحكمة لا خطأ فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings make qayyiman confirm the earlier scriptures or serve as an enduring proof.
rows.anchor: وقيل: «قيما» على الكتب السابقة يصدقها. وقيل: «قيما» بالحجج أبدا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form with kasra in awaj is used for religion, thought, affairs, and paths; with fatḥa it describes physical bodies such as wood and walls.
rows.anchor: والعوج بكسر العين في الدين والرأي والأمر والطريق. وبفتحها في الأجسام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awaj can mean flaw or contradiction; the Quran has no inconsistency, as 4:82 argues about a text from other than God.
rows.anchor:
أي ليس متناقضا مختلفا، كما قال تعالى:
ولو كان من عند غير الله لوجدوا فيه اختلافا كثيرا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas glosses 'not having awaj' as meaning the Quran is uncreated, as in 39:28.
rows.anchor:
كما روي عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى:
قرآنا عربيا غير ذي عوج

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil explains awaj as disagreement or variation.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: «عوجا» اختلافا. قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject of 'to warn' may be Muhammad or the Quran; an implied object is the disbelievers, warned of God's punishment.
rows.anchor: أي لينذر محمد أو القرآن. وفيه إضمار، أي لينذر الكافرين عقاب الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The severe punishment may occur in this world or the next; min ladunhu means from God or from His presence.
rows.anchor: وهذا العذاب الشديد قد يكون في الدنيا وقد يكون في الآخرة. { من لدنه } أي من عنده.

rows.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: Abu Bakr's reading from Asim has a still dāl with rounded articulation, a kasra on nūn, and the hā connected to a yā; other readers use a ḍamma on dāl, still nūn, and ḍamma on hā.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر عن عاصم «من لدنه» بإسكان الدال وإشمامها الضم وكسر النون،

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari lists three language forms for ladun and cites a line using lad.
rows.anchor: قال الجوهري: وفي «لدن» ثلاث لغات: لدن، ولدى، ولد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'That they have' means 'that they have a reward'; if glad tidings means clarification, the preposition bi is unnecessary.
rows.anchor: ويبشر المؤمنين الذين يعملون الصالحات أن لهم } أي بأن لهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good reward is the great recompense leading to Paradise, where the believers remain forever without an endpoint.
rows.anchor: أجرا حسنا } وهي الجنة: { ماكثين } دائمين. { فيه أبدا } لا إلى غاية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim of divine offspring includes Jews calling Uzayr God's son, Christians calling the Messiah His son, and Quraysh calling angels His daughters; this warning specifies the general warning at the sura's opening.
rows.anchor: وهم اليهود، قالوا عزير ابن الله، والنصارى قالوا المسيح ابن الله، وقريش قالت الملائكة بنات الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle min is extra; neither they nor their ancestors have knowledge or evidence for the claim, which they repeat by imitation.
rows.anchor: «من» صلة، أي ما لهم بذلك القول علم لأنهم مقلدة قالوه بغير دليل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the accusative reading, kalimatan is an explanatory apposition: that claim is a grave utterance.
rows.anchor: «كلمة» نصب على البيان أي كبرت تلك الكلمة كلمة.

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد ويحيى بن يعمر وابن أبي إسحاق
rows.claim: These readers use the nominative kalimatun, meaning the utterance itself is great, without an implied word.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ومجاهد ويحيى بن يعمر وابن أبي إسحاق «كلمة» بالرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'coming out of their mouths' functions adjectivally; their speech is only a lie.
rows.anchor: تخرج من أفواههم } في موضع الصفة. { إن يقولون إلا كذبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bakhia means destroyer or killer; athar means their traces or aftermath as they turn away, and the hadith here is the Quran.
rows.anchor: «باخع» أي مهلك وقاتل وقد تقدم. «آثارهم» جمع أثر، ويقال إثر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asafan means sorrow and anger at their disbelief, expressed as an accusative of explanation.
rows.anchor: أسفا } أي حزنا وغضبا على كفرهم وانتصب على التفسير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, ma and zinatan are both direct objects; everything on earth can be an adornment because it points to its Creator.
rows.anchor: مفعولان. والزينة كل ما على وجه الأرض فهو عموم لأنه دال على بارئه.

rows.speaker: ابن جبير عن ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: One interpretation identifies the adornment as people; the report is given through Ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas and attributed to Mujahid.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جبير عن ابن عباس: أراد بالزينة الرجال قال مجاهد.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن عكرمة
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas through Ikrima identifies the adornment as rulers and leaders.
rows.anchor: وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس أن الزينة الخلفاء والأمراء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد
rows.claim: A report through Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid says the earth's adornment is its scholars.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى: «إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض زينة لها» قال: العلماء زينة الأرض.

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group narrows the adornment to blessings, clothing, fruit, greenery, water, and similar things, excluding bare mountains and harmful creatures.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: أراد النعم والملابس والثمار والخضرة والمياه، ونحو هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi prefers the general meaning: everything on earth is an adornment through its creation, craftsmanship, and perfection.
rows.anchor: والقول بالعموم أولى، وأن كل ما على الأرض فيه زينة من جهة خلقه وصنعه وإحكامه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse consoles Muhammad: earthly display is a test of who reflects and believes and who rejects, to be repaid at resurrection, so he should not be distressed by unbelief.
rows.anchor: والآية بسط في التسلية أي لا تهتم يا محمد للدنيا وأهلها فإنا إنما جعلنا ذلك امتحانا

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Two reports from Abu Said al-Khudri compare worldly life to fresh, sweet growth and warn of the dangers in its blossoms and blessings; Muslim transmits them.
rows.anchor: إن الدنيا خضرة حلوة والله مستخلفكم فيها فينظر كيف تعملون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world is delicious to taste and pleasing to see, like attractive fruit; God tests which people do the best deeds, and only His help lets them resist what He has adorned.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: أن الدنيا مستطابة في ذوقها معجبة في منظرها كالثمر المستحلى

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar prayed for help to spend rightly what God had adorned, acknowledging that people naturally rejoice in it.
rows.anchor: اللهم إنا لا نستطيع إلا أن نفرح بما زينته لنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet compared greedy acquisition of worldly goods to someone who eats without becoming full; those consumed by accumulation face temptation and little safety, while success belongs to the contented person with sufficient provision.
rows.anchor: فمن أخذه بطيب نفس بورك له فيه ومن أخذه بإشراف نفس كان

rows.speaker: أبو ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya's father defines the best deed as lawful acquisition and spending, faith, fulfilling obligations, avoiding prohibitions, and doing abundant recommended acts.
rows.anchor: كان أبي رضي الله عنه يقول في قوله: «أحسن عملا» أحسن العمل أخذ بحق وإنفاق في حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi praises that concise definition and says the Prophet summarized it to Sufyan ibn Abd Allah: believe in God and remain upright.
rows.anchor:
آمنت بالله ثم استقم "
خرجه مسلم.

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: Al-Thawri glosses the best deed as being most ascetic toward worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقال سفيان الثوري: «أحسن عملا» أزهدهم فيها.

rows.speaker: أبو عصام العسقلاني
rows.claim: Abu Asim al-Asqalani glosses the best deed as leaving worldly life most completely.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قال أبو عصام العسقلاني: «أحسن عملا» أترك لها.

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: One definition of asceticism is short hopes, not necessarily eating coarse food or wearing a rough cloak; al-Qurtubi says this makes one content with what suffices.
rows.anchor: قصر الأمل وليس بأكل الخشن ولبس العباء قاله سفيان الثوري

rows.speaker: الأوزاعي
rows.claim: Al-Awzai's view defines asceticism as disliking commendation and praise.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: بغض المحمدة وحب الثناء. وهو قول الأوزاعي

rows.speaker: فضيل
rows.claim: Al-Fudayl's view says asceticism is abandoning the whole world, whether one likes or dislikes doing so.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: ترك الدنيا كلها هو الزهد أحب تركها أم كره. وهو قول فضيل.

rows.speaker: بشر بن الحارث
rows.claim: Bishr ibn al-Harith says love of the world means love of meeting people, while asceticism means avoiding meeting them; al-Fudayl also calls withdrawal from people a sign of asceticism.
rows.anchor: وعن بشر بن الحارث قال: حب الدنيا حب لقاء الناس، والزهد في الدنيا الزهد في لقاء الناس.

rows.speaker: إبراهيم بن أدهم
rows.claim: Ibrahim ibn Adham says one is not truly ascetic until leaving the world is more beloved than acquiring it.
rows.anchor: لا يكون الزاهد زاهدا حتى يكون ترك الدنيا أحب إليه من أخذها قاله إبراهيم بن أدهم

rows.speaker: ابن المبارك
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak defines asceticism as renunciation in the heart.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: الزهد أن تزهد في الدنيا بقلبك قاله ابن المبارك.

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group identifies asceticism with loving death.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: الزهد حب الموت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi prefers the first definition because it encompasses the substance of the other definitions.
rows.anchor: والقول الأول يعم هذه الأقوال بالمعنى فهو أولى

rows.speaker: أبو سهل
rows.claim: Abu Sahl says the earth will become soil without vegetation, as though its plants were cut away; jarz is related to cutting.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو سهل: ترابا لا نبات به كأنه قطع نباته. والجرز: القطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A barren earth has no vegetation or structures, as if all were removed; this refers to resurrection, when the ground is level and offers no shelter.
rows.anchor: والأرض الجرز التي لا نبات فيها ولا شيء من عمارة وغيرها كأنه قطع وأزيل

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas gives the lexical definition of jarz as land with no plants.
rows.anchor: النحاس: والجرز في اللغة الأرض التي لا نبات بها.

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisai says the land is jaraz when people consume every plant and crop; the derived forms describe depleted land.
rows.anchor: قال الكسائي: يقال جرزت الأرض تجرز، وجرزها القوم يجرزونها إذا أكلوا كل ما جاء فيها
